propositions: Rebar must safely delegate credential issuance, refresh, rotation, invalidation, and precedence to upstream SDKs, helpers, CI systems, and deployments rather than implementing a universal secret broker or custom credential store.

Static credentials for long-running processes (CLI, MCP, services) rotate only by restart or redeploy; Rebar does not poll environment, retrieve/refresh SSM, watch secret files, or maintain hot-reload caches.

Provider-native authentication capabilities (boto3 Session, Anthropic AccessTokenProvider, OpenAI workload identity) are injected into Rebar-owned factories; unavoidable static credentials use provider-specific non-serializable Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes containers excluded from snapshots, caches, and fingerprints.

Trusted same-capability child processes inherit ambient environment for compatibility; Rebar-materialized static credentials are overlaid only onto owning children; unrelated sibling children remove only exact Rebar-declared secret variable names; global os.environ is never mutated by Rebar.

Application-owned secrets (op-cert signing key, observability tokens) are resolved externally at process startup and supplied via REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (preferred) or multiline REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY; no runtime SSM dependency, application-owned cloud-secret retrieval, or universal get_secret() protocol is introduced.
